Hole names and copies (I2 S2): status

DFMA Review · Inventor I2, slice S2 · 2026-11-09 · branch inventor-i2-s2, draft PR #27 (not merged)

S2 is built and its checks pass. With an .ipt, each Hole feature and each thread now shows its Inventor name (Hole8, Hole20 …) in small print, but only when the name can be checked. A feature that was copied says how many of its holes were drawn and how many were copied.

Nothing to decide now. Try it in the demo. The PR waits for S3 (fillets and chamfers) and for your check of one work pair in Inventor, from 2026-11-12.

Try this

  • "nist_ctc_04_asme1_ap242-e1 (lined up) + .ipt": every Hole features row shows its name under its sizes (Hole8, Hole10, Hole11, Hole12, Hole13, Hole19, Hole20, Hole21, Hole22). Open Threads: the 4 M12 threads show Hole8.
  • CTC 04's hole findings now start with the name: "Hole20 hole on hole-12: 0.010 in [0.26 mm] off the hole's axis".
  • "nist_stc_10_asme1_ap242-e2 (lined up) + .ipt": no names at all, and the panel says "11 Hole features in the browser, 9 read." Two Holes left no trace in the file's faces, so the names can't be matched safely. hf-1 reads "4 holes: 2 drawn, 2 copied by 1 pattern or mirror feature".

The built screens

How a name is chosen

  • The .ipt stores the Hole names (Hole1, Hole2 …) apart from the holes. There is no link between them that we can read.
  • When the number of names equals the number of Hole features read, the Holes are named in order: the oldest feature gets the lowest number. Otherwise no Hole gets a name. A renamed Hole ("Mounting holes") is not a default name, so that part shows none. It is never a guess.
  • Checked against the answer key on the NIST files: 70 of 70 right, 0 wrong. On FTC 06 2024 and STC 10 the counts differ, so they show no names.
  • The risk: two faults in one file could cancel out and shift every name by one. Only a check in Inventor can catch that. Your work-pair check, with one Hole renamed, is that test before the PR merges.

Checks

  • scripts/check.py: all passed (771 service tests, web check and build, 38 browser tests).
  • A fresh review against the spec found no blockers. Fixed: 4 missing tests, a stale comment, and thread naming moved into one tested function. Left as the spec says: the risk above.
  • One full run hit the 10 s limit on the slowest NIST file (10.1 s). Main itself takes 10.1 to 10.9 s on it in this container, so the container is slow, not S2. The limit is unchanged and the re-runs passed.
